recommended.title: Corrective, re-run: auth integration decision, with a forgeable profile scope and an unsupported pin
recommended.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0401. It carries three merits blockers as well as a provenance correction, and the merits are the larger half. PROVENANCE: PL-0401 recorded implementationBaseSha fc1ea4d54c9e7d2b2f6d9aa71a977abdc3bcb400, proven with ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES. Those witnesses correctly located the code introduction and missed earlier task implementation on another declared write path: docs/DATA_MODEL.md did not exist at 56b343 and was created in bbe68ed8, before the recorded base, already identifying itself as covering this task's auth boundary and already selecting Better Auth 1.7.1. The true lower bound is 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7 while docs/DATA_MODEL.md remains a write surface. PL-0401 is BLOCKED with the false range preserved as audit history. DO NOT CLAIM THIS TASK UNTIL THE THREE BLOCKERS IN THE NOTES ARE IMPLEMENTED; it is created now so the findings are recorded against a task rather than living only in a review transcript.
recommended.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. THE SURFACE THIS IMPLIES IS WIDER THAN THIS TASK CURRENTLY DECLARES, AND THAT IS SETTLED BEFORE THE CLAIM RATHER THAN DISCOVERED DURING IT. The reviewer offered two levels: at minimum make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability, use issuance identity as well. The minimum is NOT ACHIEVABLE IN THE TYPE SYSTEM, and PL-0706 already established why: a spread copies a branded property along with everything else and type-checks with no cast at all, so only object identity rejects it. TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable. Therefore the runtime registry is not the optional upper level here, it is the only level that works -- and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ASK. The consumers are in another package: packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts and watchlist-repository.ts read scope.profileId straight into their predicates, and profile-repository.ts and repository-scoping.test.ts also handle the type. So this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration, and it will then overlap PL-0402, PL-0403 and PL-0404, which are BACKLOG today and must be sequenced after it. The alternative -- brand and registry in packages/auth with no consumer asking -- would produce a capability that looks unforgeable and is not, which is worse than the present state because it would read as fixed. Whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. DO NOT BUMP AND LEAVE THE MIGRATION: 1.7.3 restored the 1.6 account core schema after the issuer-schema change in 1.7.0 through 1.7.2, while this repository's hand-written migration still has an issuer column and an (issuer, account_id) uniqueness rule. The migration must be regenerated or reconciled against the reviewed version BEFORE security approval. That is why packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql moves from reviewDependency to WRITE PATH here: on PL-0401 it was only evidence, and read-only was correct; here it has to change, and reviewDependencies are read-only by contract. PL-0402 also owns packages/persistence and is BACKLOG, so no active conflict exists today, but the two must be sequenced and the reviewer should say which owns that file afterwards. BLOCKER 3. ADR-007 still states obsolete control-plane routing, naming gpt-architect as preferred implementer and claude-lead as reviewer, while the record now correctly has claude-backend implementing and gpt-architect reviewing independently. Rewrite that paragraph as history rather than as current routing, and prefer wording that points at the task gate as authoritative -- otherwise completing the review needs a post-approval edit that immediately stales the fingerprint it just bound. TWO HONEST CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD FROM PL-0401, neither an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed, because no PostgreSQL exists in this environment, and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. SEQUENCING: this task is READY rather than BLOCKED because nothing external gates it, but it should not be claimed until the three blockers are implemented, and claiming it early would reserve packages/auth and two documents while no work was happening.
recommended.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range. The pinned version must be one upstream currently supports, and the hand-written migration must agree with that version's account schema rather than an abandoned intermediate one. ProfileScope must be UNFORGEABLE by a holder of a genuine scope: a spread copy carrying a replaced profileId must not remain assignable, and any consumer that grants data access on the strength of a scope must establish that the scope was ISSUED rather than merely that it type-checks. The decision record must describe the routing that actually applies, or point at the task record as authoritative rather than restating it.

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.
